transcript.text: roomba e5 wont charge properly, sometimes it does sometimes it doesnt

This "intermittent charging" issue is one of the most common problems with the Roomba i3/e5 series (which share similar hardware). It usually points to a dirty connection or a sensor blockage rather than a dead battery.

Here’s a step-by-step troubleshooting guide, ordered from most likely to least likely cause:

### 1. Clean the Charging Contacts (Most Common Fix)
The metal contacts on both the Roomba and the charging base can accumulate dust, hair, or oxidize over time, causing poor electrical connection.
• On the Roomba: Locate the two gold-colored metal strips near the rear wheels. Wipe them firmly with a dry microfiber cloth or a cotton swab dipped in isopropyl alcohol (rubbing alcohol). Let them dry completely.
• On the Charging Base: Clean the corresponding metal contacts on the base station using the same method. Ensure the power cable is securely plugged into both the wall and the base.

### 2. Check for "False" Docking
The Roomba may think it has docked when it hasn’t made proper contact with the charging pins.
• Reposition the Base: Move the charging base away from walls or furniture by at least 1.5 feet (0.5 meters) on each side and 3 feet (0.9 meters) in front. The Roomba needs space to approach straight on.
• Check for Obstructions: Ensure no rugs, cords, or low furniture are blocking the path. Thick shag rugs can prevent the wheels from reaching the base fully.
• Manually Dock It: When the battery is low (red light), manually place the Roomba on the charging base. Listen for a chime and check if the green "Charge" light turns on. If it works when placed manually but not autonomously, your docking station location is likely the issue.

### 3. Reset the Charging Base
Sometimes the base’s internal logic gets confused.
• Unplug the charging base from the wall outlet.
• Wait for 60 seconds.
• Plug it back in and wait for the light to stabilize (usually solid green or blue, depending on model).

### 4. Check the Battery Health
If cleaning and repositioning don’t help, the battery may be failing. The e5 uses a lithium-ion battery that typically lasts 2–3 years.
• Symptoms of a dying battery: It charges to only 10–20% and dies quickly, or it refuses to hold a charge even after being on the base for hours.
• Test: Let it charge fully (green light solid), then run a cleaning cycle. If it shuts down unexpectedly before the bin is full or the area is cleaned, the battery likely needs replacement.

### 5. Firmware Update
An outdated firmware can cause charging logic errors.
• Open the iRobot Home App.
• Go to your Roomba e5 > Settings > Check for Updates.
• If an update is available, install it while the Roomba is on the charger.

### 6. Hard Reset the Roomba
If software glitches are suspected:
1.  Remove the battery (slide the release latch and lift it out).
2.  Wait 30 seconds.
3.  Reinsert the battery firmly.
4.  Press and hold the Home button for 5–10 seconds until you hear a series of tones or see the lights flash.

---

### When to Contact Support
If none of the above works:
• The Roomba may have a faulty charging port on the unit itself.
• The battery may be completely dead and need replacement (iRobot sells official replacements, or third-party options are available).
• If your Roomba is under 1 year old, it’s likely still under warranty.

Quick Tip: Try running the Roomba on a hard floor (not carpet) while docked. Sometimes thick carpets insulate the charging contacts slightly, preventing full connection.
